# Private generated files

GH-0601 introduces the server-side `@green-hive/files` boundary for generated private artifacts.
It is deliberately metadata-first: it stores an opaque object locator and lifecycle evidence, while
returning owners only the reviewed file metadata necessary to list an artifact.

## Public contract

`FileService` exposes `storeGenerated`, `list`, `get` and `softDelete`. It accepts a verified
`TrustedOrganizationContext` plus generated bytes, project UUID, idempotency key, original
filename and MIME type. Callers cannot supply an owner, organization, app, status, provider,
bucket, storage key, hash, capability or object version.

The owner-visible `FileRecord` contains only identifier, project, filename, MIME type, byte size,
sensitivity, ready state and timestamps. It never exposes a storage URL, provider, bucket, object
key, content hash, entitlement identity, idempotency hash or object version.

## Lifecycle and isolation

Migration `0023` adds `hive.files` with an opaque database-generated key of the form
`ghf/<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>`. Original filenames are metadata only and are never
used as paths. A composite foreign key binds each row to one owner, workspace, installed app and
project. The lifecycle is:

```text
prepare (PROCESSING) -> private object write -> complete (READY) -> soft delete (DELETED)
```

The prepare function repeats trusted user/app/workspace/project checks, requires an active
manifest-backed `REFERENCE_APP_GENERATE_FILE` entitlement and calculates/replays idempotency from
hashed server inputs. A changed request under the same idempotency key is rejected. If object
writing or completion fails, the service compensates only the in-flight processing metadata and
private object that it owns.

`authenticated` receives safe-column `SELECT` only. There is no direct `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or
`DELETE`, no lifecycle function grant and no platform-admin bypass. The service-role-only writers
have a fixed empty SQL search path and independently repeat authorization. A deleted object is
not returned to its owner; its metadata remains retained for controlled operational recovery.

## Storage adapters

`FakeFileStorage` is deterministic, in-memory and zero-network; it is the default test adapter.
`SupabasePrivateStorageProvider` is an injected server-only adapter that accepts only configured
private bucket names and opaque keys, writes content integrity metadata, reconciles idempotent
replays and has no method for public or signed URLs. Credentials and client construction remain
outside the package and must never be browser-accessible.

The local Supabase stack intentionally keeps Storage disabled today. That protects the existing
minimal development surface while the adapter remains covered with a strict client double. A real
private-bucket activation is an explicit operational follow-up, not an automatic deployment side
effect and not a reason to expose a public bucket.

## Deliberately deferred

GH-0601 does not create a browser upload endpoint, accept arbitrary user uploads, issue public or
signed download links, enable a public bucket, scan files, run rendering, write a `FILE_EXPORTED`
Audit event, configure CDN/cache delivery or activate remote Storage in staging. GH-0602 owns the
authorized expiring download path; GH-0603 owns generic PDF/text rendering and storage composition.
